title: the WSG World of Weather appendix, part 2 - special weather, the effects on play and the optional rules
audit_comment: The Appendix: The World of Weather, part 2 of 2 - the special weather system and the effects on play, printed pp. 112-119. Table A4 with the Roll 1 / Roll 2 cross-index (the 2-or-12 carry-over, the fresh 2d6, the five bands and the 1st-2nd-3rd-4th letter selection, the running-episode suppression), the 33-row x 4-season special weather grid (one packed four-letter code per cell: cold wave, cyclone, drought, gale, mist/fog, sandstorm, tornado, extreme precipitation, heat wave). The per-code definitions: the no-special 2 and 12 days (the 45 mph very strong wind with the sharp drop, the 5 mph very slight wind with the sharp rise, the B-column precipitation), the cold wave and its heat wave mirror (2d6+2 days, 4 steps per day, the floor and ceiling one step beyond the normal extreme, the 10-degree beyond-extreme cap for 3 days, the automatic recovery with the 7-or-higher bonus rise), the cyclone (the 1d6x20+60 mph wind, the seacoast lightning herald, the 10-mile inland reach and 50-mile perimeter, the away-from-equator and coast-following movement, the double downpour, the 3-mile tidal wave, the 6-hour eye with its half-hour-to-hour dead calm, the second-half rainstorm, the 10-mph eye wind, the 3-day no-change-table window with the two-day 2d6 drift, the once-per-month 200-mile frequency cap with the extreme-precipitation fallback, the 5-degree equator exclusion), the drought (2d6+2 days, the day-1 shutoff, the once-per-5-days trace, the heavy-to-light-to-trace-to-none ladder), the gale (1d6x5+40 mph for 1d6+1 hours, the never-below-30 rule, the previous-20 boost, the desert and snow severe-sandstorm readings), the mist/fog (the sunrise/sunset 1-4/5-6 split, the 1d6 hours, the seacoast heavy reading, the suspended precipitation, the 50-percent adjacent spread), the sandstorm (the loose-material requirement, the no-precipitation day, the 1d4+1 and severe 1d6+1 durations), the tornado (the suitable-conditions and two-steps-above gates, the 1d3-hour front, the abrupt stop, the half-mile calm, the 3d6-minute delay, the 15-degrees-or-3-steps drop over 30 minutes, the quarter-by-15-mile path at 40 mph, the 200-300 mph vortex, the low-pressure explosion), the extreme precipitation dispatch (7 temperature bands x 2 climatic columns x the 1d6 sub-roll, the 25-degree ice footnote) and its four payloads: the hailstorm (the first-10-minutes-of-lightning rule, the 1-on-1d6 standalone, the 1d6+4 minutes, the quarter-inch stones to 2-3 inches, the 40-degree melt), the ice storm (the half-to-three-quarter-inch coating, the 20-minute heavy and 2-hour trace formation), the lightning storm (25 minutes, three-quarters-to-1 inch of rain, the dawn/dusk window, the disregarded standalone under moderate or light, the downpour start) and the severe snowstorm (the 1d6+4 and 1d6+6 inch falls at 1 inch per hour, the 1-2-hour calm then the 15-20 mph wind). The optional rules: the Table A5 humidity variation grid with the letter codes and their percentage bands, the day 1 / day 2 adjustment with the before and after slash pairs, the three-level fluctuation range with the dry and saturated edges and the two-level DM drop, the Table A6 humidity and effective temperature grid (25 rows x 5 wind columns, applied at 60 degrees and above), the Table A7 wind chill grid (17 x 8) with the below-minus-45 extrapolation and the 40-mph wind column cap, the Table A8 hours of daylight grid (15 latitude rows x 12 months, stored in half-hours) with the simplified middle-row option and the midnight/noon midpoint convention, the twilight spans (30 minutes at 30-40 degrees, 20 at the equator, 40 at 50-60, the 5-10-minute terrain cut, the all-day twilight where the daylight reads zero), the local winds (the sea breeze by day and the land breeze by night, the 5-10-mile inland reach, the clear-sky favor, the coastal chill, the cliff-face trap), the tides (the twice-daily alternation, the 12-hour highs and 6-hour lows, the 25-hour lunar day with the hour-a-day advance, the 28-day cycle, the spring and neap windows, the 5-7 and 15-18 foot ranges, the Fundy 60, the gentle/moderate/severe slope encroachment multiples with both worked examples) and the Dungeon Master responsibility (the 2-3-day determinations, the free timeframe switching, the multi-day predetermination).

banner.sentinel: THE SETTLE: Table A4 is the psm-6 read win - default tesseract, pdftotext and the djvu reads all garble the grid, and the 400-dpi psm-6 pass decodes it letter-for-letter with the TSV confidences checked per cell; the port agrees cell-for-cell on 28 of 33 rows and the djvu corroborates the arctic, temperate and subtropical interior blocks. Cyclone is confirmed on the coasts: the temperate seacoast spring/summer cells read CXMZ in three independent sources against the port uniform AXMZ, and the same coastal warm-season pattern carries the subtropical seacoast and swamp spring/summer cells and the tropical seacoast summer cell (flagged - that C is a low-confidence read). The swamp rows are psm-6 only (the port has no swamp biome and the djvu drops them), and the tropical swamp winter cell is the single inferred cell of the grid (the ANz D glyph read, decoded by the all-Z fourth-letter pattern of the tropical winter column). The A5 humidity grid rides the same 33-row model as A4 (the printed arctic-all-terrains line expanded to its five terrain rows); the transcription wins the two subarctic cells where the port rotation disagrees, the A3 precedent. A6 and A7 are transcription-port exact; A8 is 15 latitude rows (the earlier 16-row note was a miscount), cross-checked against the pdf layout read; the prose pages read clean throughout.

consts.name: wwyA8Lat6
consts.comment: row 6: 50 degrees; rows 7-8 are 40 and 35 (the temperate block).

consts.name: wwyA8Lat9
consts.comment: row 9: 30 degrees; rows 10-11 are 25 and 20 (the subtropical block).

consts.name: wwyA8Lat12
consts.comment: row 12: 15 degrees; rows 13-14 are 10 and 0 (the tropical block).

consts.name: wwyA8Lat14
consts.comment: row 14: the equator, 12 hours of daylight every day of the year.

consts.name: wwyTwilightMidLatMin
consts.comment: each of the two daily twilight periods lasts about 30 minutes at the middle latitudes.

consts.name: wwyTwilightMidLatLoDeg
consts.comment: the middle-latitude band: 30-40 degrees.

consts.name: wwyTwilightMidLatHiDeg
consts.comment: the middle-latitude band ceiling.

consts.name: wwyTwilightEquatorMin
consts.comment: twilight decreases to a minimum of 20 minutes at the equator.

consts.name: wwyTwilightHighLatMin
consts.comment: twilight increases to 40 minutes at relatively high latitudes.

consts.name: wwyTwilightHighLatLoDeg
consts.comment: the high-latitude band: 50-60 degrees.

consts.name: wwyTwilightHighLatHiDeg
consts.comment: the high-latitude band ceiling.

consts.name: wwyTwilightTerrainMinLo
consts.comment: local terrain can cut twilight to 5-10 minutes (a dense forest, the shaded side of a mountain).

consts.name: wwyTwilightTerrainMinHi
consts.comment: the terrain-cut twilight ceiling.

consts.name: wwySeaBreezeInlandMinMi
consts.comment: a sea breeze reaches 5-10 miles inland.

consts.name: wwySeaBreezeInlandMaxMi
consts.comment: the sea-breeze inland reach ceiling.

consts.name: wwyTideHoursBetweenHighs
consts.comment: there are two high tides and two low tides daily, alternating; about 12 hours pass between one high tide and the next.

consts.name: wwyTideLowAfterHighHrs
consts.comment: low tide comes about 6 hours after high tide.

consts.name: wwyLunarDayRoughHrs
consts.comment: the lunar day runs about 25 hours, so the whole tidal cycle advances about an hour later each day.

consts.name: wwyTideAdvanceMinPerDay
consts.comment: the daily tidal advance, pinned in minutes.

consts.name: wwyTideCycleDays
consts.comment: the full tidal cycle repeats with the 28-day lunar cycle.

consts.name: wwySpringWindowDays
consts.comment: spring tides occur in roughly 7-day windows around the full and new moon; the rest of the cycle is neap tides.

consts.name: wwyNeapRangeFtLo
consts.comment: an average neap tide runs 5-7 feet from high to low.

consts.name: wwyNeapRangeFtHi
consts.comment: the neap range ceiling.

consts.name: wwySpringRangeFtLo
consts.comment: an average spring tide runs 15-18 feet from high to low.

consts.name: wwySpringRangeFtHi
consts.comment: the spring range ceiling.

consts.name: wwyFundyMaxFt
consts.comment: extreme coastal configurations can multiply the range (the Bay of Fundy reaches 60 feet).

consts.name: wwyGentleSlopeMaxDeg
consts.comment: tidal encroachment on a gently sloped shore (30 degrees or less): the water encroaches 4-5 times the tide height.

consts.name: wwyGentleEncroachLoX
consts.comment: the gentle-slope encroachment low multiple.

consts.name: wwyGentleEncroachHiX
consts.comment: the gentle-slope encroachment high multiple.

consts.name: wwyModerateSlopeLoDeg
consts.comment: a moderately sloped shore runs 31-50 degrees.

consts.name: wwyModerateSlopeHiDeg
consts.comment: the moderate-slope ceiling.

consts.name: wwyModerateEncroachLoX
consts.comment: the moderate-slope encroachment: 2-3 times the tide height.

consts.name: wwyModerateEncroachHiX
consts.comment: the moderate-slope high multiple.

consts.name: wwySevereSlopeLoDeg
consts.comment: a severely sloped shore runs 51-70 degrees.

consts.name: wwySevereSlopeHiDeg
consts.comment: the severe-slope ceiling.

consts.name: wwySevereEncroachLoX
consts.comment: the severe-slope encroachment: 1-2 times the tide height.

consts.name: wwySevereEncroachHiX
consts.comment: the severe-slope high multiple.

consts.name: wwyTideExampleGentleFt
consts.comment: the worked gentle-slope example: a 15-foot spring high tide.

consts.name: wwyTideExampleGentleEncroachLoFt
consts.comment: the example encroaches 60-75 feet (4 x 15 to 5 x 15).

consts.name: wwyTideExampleGentleEncroachHiFt
consts.comment: the example ceiling.

consts.name: wwyTideExampleModerateFt
consts.comment: the worked moderate-slope example: a 5-foot tide.

consts.name: wwyTideExampleModerateEncroachLoFt
consts.comment: the example encroaches 10-15 feet (2 x 5 to 3 x 5).

consts.name: wwyTideExampleModerateEncroachHiFt
consts.comment: the example ceiling.

bools.name: wwyRunningEpisodeNoSpecial
bools.comment: if any special weather episode is already in progress, a roll of 2 or 12 on the Day-to-Day Change Table indicates no special weather for that day.

bools.name: wwyNoSpecRoll2SharpDrop
bools.comment: the no-special 2: the temperature takes a sharp drop.

bools.name: wwyNoSpecRoll2PrecipB
bools.comment: the no-special 2: precipitation is possible, as given on the Precipitation Variation Table for a roll of doubles (the B column).

bools.name: wwyNoSpecRoll2WindSource50
bools.comment: the no-special 2: the wind comes from the arctic or from the prevailing direction, 50 percent either way.

bools.name: wwyNoSpecRoll12SharpRise
bools.comment: the no-special 12: the temperature takes a sharp rise.

bools.name: wwyNoSpecRoll12PrecipB
bools.comment: the no-special 12: precipitation is possible, as given on the Precipitation Variation Table for a roll of doubles (the B column).

bools.name: wwyColdWaveFloorBelowMin
bools.comment: the daily drop stops one step below the normal minimum temperature for the date (the wave floor).

bools.name: wwyColdWaveRecoveryAutoRise
bools.comment: the recovery from a cold wave is automatic: the temperature rises to the normal minimum with no roll.

bools.name: wwyHeatWaveCeilingAboveMax
bools.comment: the daily rise stops one step above the normal maximum temperature for the date (the wave ceiling).

bools.name: wwyHeatWaveRecoveryAutoFall
bools.comment: the recovery from a heat wave is automatic: the temperature falls to the normal maximum with no roll.

bools.name: wwyCycloneSeacoastLightningDayBefore
bools.comment: at a seacoast, a cyclone is heralded a day in advance by a lightning storm.

bools.name: wwyCycloneMovesAwayFromEquator
bools.comment: a cyclone moves away from the equator (toward the nearest pole).

bools.name: wwyCycloneFollowsCoast
bools.comment: at sea a cyclone follows the coastline rather than striking inland directly.

bools.name: wwyCycloneRainDoubleDownpour
bools.comment: within the cyclone the rain is at least twice that of a downpour.

bools.name: wwyCycloneEyeSecondHalfRainstorm
bools.comment: the second half of the eye brings a heavy rainstorm for its 6 hours.

bools.name: wwyCycloneMaxOncePerMonth
bools.comment: an area can be struck by at most one cyclone in a given month.

bools.name: wwyCycloneSecondBecomesExtreme
bools.comment: a second cyclone indicated within the 200-mile radius in the same month indicates extreme precipitation instead.

bools.name: wwyCycloneNotNearEquator
bools.comment: cyclones are not generated within 5 degrees of the equator.

bools.name: wwyDroughtDay1NoPrecip
bools.comment: no precipitation falls on the first day of a drought.

bools.name: wwyDroughtLightToTrace
bools.comment: precipitation indicated at light or moderate maximum falls as at most a trace during a drought.

bools.name: wwyDroughtHeavyLadder
bools.comment: heavy-maximum precipitation steps down each day of the drought: heavy to light, moderate to trace, light to none.

bools.name: wwyGaleNeverBelow30
bools.comment: wind velocity during a gale never drops below 30 mph and is mostly 50 mph or greater.

bools.name: wwyGalePrev20Boost
bools.comment: if the previous day wind was 20 mph or greater, the gale reads 50-70 mph.

bools.name: wwyGaleDesertSandstorm
bools.comment: in a desert a gale produces no precipitation and whips up a severe sandstorm instead.

bools.name: wwyGaleSnowSevereSandstorm
bools.comment: in an arctic or subarctic climate (or anywhere with snow on the ground) a gale whips the snow into a severe blizzard, the blowing-snow analogue of a severe sandstorm.

bools.name: wwyMistHeavyNearWater
bools.comment: in a seacoast area or an area adjacent to a large body of water the fog is heavy; elsewhere it is moderate.

bools.name: wwyMistSuspendsPrecip
bools.comment: precipitation is suspended while the mist or fog lasts.

bools.name: wwyMistAdjacent50
bools.comment: there is a 50 percent chance of mist or fog the day before and the day after in an area adjacent to the fog.

bools.name: wwySandstormNeedsLooseMaterial
bools.comment: a sandstorm requires an area of loose soil, sand or snow (fine dirt also qualifies).

bools.name: wwySandstormNoPrecipThatDay
bools.comment: no precipitation falls on the day of a sandstorm.

bools.name: wwyTornadoConditionsSuitable
bools.comment: a tornado occurs only when conditions are suitable: only in areas where tornados are known to occur, and only during special weather determinations.

bools.name: wwyTornadoTempTwoStepsAbove
bools.comment: a tornado requires the temperature to be at least 2 steps above normal for the day.

bools.name: wwyTornadoRainStopsAbruptly
bools.comment: the heavy rain of the tornado front stops abruptly as the tornado approaches.

bools.name: wwyTornadoCalmNearPath
bools.comment: within one-half mile of the tornado path the air is calm.

bools.name: wwyTornadoDropGreater
bools.comment: the 15-degree or 3-step temperature drop takes the greater of the two measures.

bools.name: wwyTornadoCalmRestOfDay
bools.comment: after the tornado passes the calm lasts the rest of the day.

bools.name: wwyTornadoLowPressureExplosion
bools.comment: the extremely low air pressure inside the vortex can cause sealed structures to explode.

bools.name: wwyExtremePrecipSubroll
bools.comment: when the code letter X is selected, cross-index the temperature with the climatic column and roll 1d6 on the dispatch table to determine the type of extreme precipitation.

bools.name: wwyXDisIceNeeds25F
bools.comment: in the 10-29 band the ice/sleet result of the dispatch carries the 25-degree minimum-temperature requirement.

bools.name: wwyLightningHalfAtTwilight
bools.comment: lightning storms favor the dawn and dusk windows: about half fall within two hours either side of sunrise or sunset.

bools.name: wwyLightningStandaloneDisregarded
bools.comment: a lightning result on the dispatch under moderate or light precipitation maximums is disregarded (it rides the stronger storm types).

bools.name: wwyLightningAtDownpourStart
bools.comment: in a downpour the lightning storm occurs at the start of the precipitation.

bools.name: wwySevereSnowWindAfter
bools.comment: a severe snowstorm starts calm and turns windy: after 1-2 hours of snow the wind rises to very strong, 15-20 mph.

bools.name: wwyHumFluctuatesOneLevel
bools.comment: humidity fluctuates one level to either side of the Table A5 level as weather changes (a three-level range).

bools.name: wwyHumLowEdgeDry
bools.comment: a fluctuation below low reads dry (0-20 percent).

bools.name: wwyHumHighEdgeSaturated
bools.comment: a fluctuation above high reads saturated (91-100 percent).

bools.name: wwyHumDMTwoLevelDrop
bools.comment: the Dungeon Master may allow a two-level drop in exceptional conditions (a cold front after a rainstorm).

bools.name: wwyChillExtrapBelow
bools.comment: for temperatures lower than -45, extrapolate downward following the pattern of the decrease from -40 to -45.

bools.name: wwyChillExtrapAbove40Mph
bools.comment: for wind speeds greater than 40 mph, use the 40-mph column; greater wind speeds have little if any additional chilling effect.

bools.name: wwyA8SimplifiedRowsOnly
bools.comment: the shorter simplified version uses only the middle row of each climatic block: the 80 line for arctic, 60 for subarctic, 40 for temperate, 25 for subtropical, 10 for tropical - no latitude bookkeeping, only the climatic region.

bools.name: wwyA8MidnightNightMidpoint
bools.comment: the table gives lengths, not clock times: sunrise and sunset are derived with midnight as the midpoint of the nighttime period and noon as the midpoint of the daytime period, or stipulated by the Dungeon Master.

bools.name: wwyTwilightAllDayWhereNoDaylight
bools.comment: where the daylight table reads zero, the day is not black: the period is one of twilight, not true darkness (the arctic winter).

bools.name: wwySeaBreezeDayWaterToLand
bools.comment: during the day the land heats faster than the water: a sea breeze blows from the water toward the land.

bools.name: wwyLandBreezeNight
bools.comment: at night the land cools faster: a land breeze blows from the land toward the water.

bools.name: wwySeaBreezeStronger
bools.comment: the daytime sea breeze is stronger than the nighttime land breeze.

bools.name: wwyClearSkiesFavorBreezes
bools.comment: clear skies favor both breezes (maximum heating and cooling differential); cloud cover reduces them.

bools.name: wwySeaBreezeCanChillCoast
bools.comment: a sea breeze can lower the coastal temperature by as much as 20 degrees on a hot day (the Lake Michigan breeze).

bools.name: wwyCliffFacesTrapSwirlCalm
bools.comment: in the lee of a cliff face the wind swirls, is trapped, or dies to a calm - local terrain dominates over the regional wind.

bools.name: wwyTidesTwiceDailyAlternating
bools.comment: the two daily tides alternate high and low, in equal numbers of high and low waters.

bools.name: wwySpringTidesAroundFullNew
bools.comment: spring tides (the stronger tides) fall in the windows around the full and the new moon; neap tides fill the rest of the cycle.

bools.name: wwyDMDetermine2to3Days
bools.comment: the Dungeon Master determines the weather 2-3 days in advance of the play session, keeping the determination hidden until it comes into play.

bools.name: wwyDMSwitchTimeframesFreely
bools.comment: the DM switches freely between determining weather one day at a time, several days at once, or whole weeks - whatever the pace of play demands.

bools.name: wwyDMPredetermineMultiDay
bools.comment: for multi-day outings (long journeys, expeditions) the DM predetermines the weather for the entire span before play begins.

chains.name: wwyCycloneDriftFor
chains.comment: the two-day drift after a cyclone: each day roll 2d6 - 6 or less drops the temperature 1 step (band 0), 7 holds it (band 1), 8 or higher raises it 1 step (band 2).

the selected letter for the Roll 2 band 5-6 (row 0: Roll 1 = 2 picks the 2nd letter; row 1: Roll 1 = 12 picks none)

the selected letter for the Roll 2 band 8-9 (row 0: Roll 1 = 2 picks none; row 1: Roll 1 = 12 picks the 3rd)

tables.name: wwyA4Special
col_comments: the four-letter code for Winter (the packed digits, one letter per digit: A=1 cold wave, C=2 cyclone, D=3 drought, G=4 gale, M=5 mist/fog, S=6 sandstorm, T=7 tornado, X=8 extreme precipitation, Z=9 heat wave)
tables.audit_comment: the Table A4 grid: 33 climate/terrain rows x the four seasonal codes, each cell a packed four-letter code (arctic rows 0-4, subarctic 5-11, temperate 12-18, subtropical 19-25, tropical 26-32; desert, forest, hills, mountains, plains, seacoast, swamp within each block)

tables.name: wwyXDispatch
tables.audit_comment: the X dispatch: 7 temperature bands x the 1-6 sub-rolls for the two climatic columns (values 1 hail, 2 ice/sleet, 3 lightning, 4 severe snowstorm, 0 none; the 10-29 band ice cell carries the 25-degree footnote)

tables.name: wwyA5Humidity
col_comments: the humidity level for Winter (1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high)
tables.audit_comment: the Table A5 humidity grid: 33 climate/terrain rows x the four seasonal levels (the arctic block uniformly low, printed order Winter/Spring/Summer/Autumn)

col_comments: the humidity step adjustment taken BEFORE the day 2 precipitation, day 2 column none
the day 2 column light or trace
the day 2 column medium or more
tables.audit_comment: the day 1 / day 2 humidity adjustment, the BEFORE halves of the printed slash pairs

tables.name: wwyHumAdjAfter
col_comments: the humidity step adjustment taken AFTER the day 2 precipitation, day 2 column none
the day 2 column light or trace
the day 2 column medium or more
tables.audit_comment: the day 1 / day 2 humidity adjustment, the AFTER halves of the printed slash pairs

tables.name: wwyA6EffectiveTemp
col_comments: the effective-temperature adjustment at wind 0-10 mph
tables.audit_comment: the Table A6 grid: rows are the 5 temperature bands x the 5 humidity levels in the order dry, low, medium, high, saturated; the values are the degrees added to the actual temperature for effective temperature

tables.name: wwyA7WindChill
col_comments: the effective temperature at 5 mph wind
tables.audit_comment: the Table A7 wind chill grid: 17 temperature rows (35 down to -45 by 5) x 8 wind columns (5 to 40 by 5)

col_comments: the hours of daylight in month 1 (in half-hours: 48 = 24 hours)
the hours of daylight in month 2
the hours of daylight in month 3
the hours of daylight in month 4
the hours of daylight in month 5
the hours of daylight in month 6
the hours of daylight in month 7
the hours of daylight in month 8
the hours of daylight in month 9

the settle: the temperate seacoast spring and summer cells carry the cyclone (three independent reads against the port uniform AXMZ)
the settle: the psm-6 swamp rows - subtropical swamp mirrors the subtropical seacoast (AXDZ CXMZ CXMZ AXDZ)
the settle: the inferred tropical swamp winter cell (the A-N-z-D glyph read decoded by the all-Z tropical winter fourth-letter pattern)
the arctic desert is uniform GADD across all four seasons
the Roll 1 = 12 / Roll 2 = 7 example: the third letter
the X dispatch at 75+ degrees in the tropics: lightning on any sub-roll
the X dispatch below zero in the temperate column: snow on 1-3, none on 4-6

the arctic pole: total darkness in month 1, total daylight in month 6
the temperate seacoast humidity: HMMH in every season
